title: Rule resolution applicability register
description: One record per agent-norm intake entry states the axes on which the resolver decides whether that norm reaches a given work item (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §5). A record does not carry the norm's text or its intake verdict: it carries a qualified reference to where the norm is recorded, the digest the resolver checks for staleness, an unambiguous pointer to the one append-only intake record it is synced to, and this record's own runtime-applicability status. The intake verdict (deferred, keep-local, adopt-core, …), its verdict_basis and its own resume_condition are read by joining on that pointer, not copied here: standards/workspace/kernel-boundary.md's rule that Instance stores links, not copies, applies to applicability data the same way it applies to instruction-intake.md's own derived_from. Runtime applicability has exactly two states — resolved and unresolved — and is not the intake verdict: a deferred intake verdict does not by itself make a record unresolved, activate it, or disable it (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §4). Absence of a record is not how an undecidable norm is represented — a norm whose scope, activation or source cannot be decided deterministically is present here with status "unresolved" and its own resume_condition, so that the resolver returns unresolved_applicability for it from an explicit status, never from a missing entry. The axis named architecture_profile in standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §5.2 is deliberately absent: the owner decided not to introduce it as a schema field for the MVP, and its storage form remains open for a future revision of this schema, not a silent addition to this one; additionalProperties:false below refuses it until then.

records.description: One entry per intake record in the MVP perimeter, represented individually — including every record whose intake verdict is deferred and every record the axes below cannot resolve. There is no group status: the count of deferred intake records is a counter, not a shared resume trigger (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §9), so each record carries its own status, its own resume_condition when unresolved, and its own intake_record pointer, and is resumed on its own condition, never on another record's.

norm.description: Qualified reference to where the norm's text is recorded — the same shape as derived_from in registries/instruction-intake/intake.schema.json, reused rather than reinvented. This names where the text lives, which is independent of which repository the applicability axes below say it applies to: a norm found in one repository's intake register can be scoped to a whole technology profile, or to no repository in particular.

repository.description: Repository identifier from the Instance inventory, or "kernel" for a norm that lives in the Meridian Kernel and never went through instruction-intake.

path.description: Path relative to that repository's root, or to the Kernel root when repository is "kernel".

region.description: Identifier of a declared region inside a container file (instruction-intake.md §3.1), present only when the norm is one participant of a container rather than a whole artifact. When present it is part of the pointer to the one intake record this applicability entry is synced to.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the norm's text as it stood when this applicability record was last synced to it — of the file's bytes when norm.region is absent, of the region's text under instruction-intake.md §7.1 when it is present. A norm whose current digest no longer matches this value has moved since this record was written; that is a staleness finding for whoever reads the record, not a value this schema can check by itself.

intake_record.description: Unambiguous pointer to the one append-only instruction-intake record this applicability entry is synced to. It reuses the record identity instruction-intake.md already defines and the gate already keys on — artifact + region + recorded_at + verdict — it does not invent a parallel one: norm.path is the artifact and norm.region the region, so this object adds register (which file), recorded_at (which revision date) and verdict (which of possibly several entries made on that date). recorded_at alone does not identify a record: one artifact and region can carry more than one entry on the same date with different verdicts, and only the full tuple picks one out. The intake verdict, its verdict_basis and its own resume_condition are then read from that one record, not copied here. Required when source is repository or delivery-adapter; forbidden when source is kernel, because a norm that never went through intake has no intake record to point at.

register.description: Path to the instruction-intake/*.yaml register file that carries the record, relative to the Instance root.

recorded_at.description: The recorded_at of that one append-only intake record. It is one component of the record identity, not the whole of it — norm.path, norm.region and verdict are the others.

verdict.description: The verdict of that one intake record, from the pool in registries/instruction-intake/intake.schema.json. Part of the record identity: two entries for one artifact and region on one date are told apart by verdict. Carrying it here is a pointer component, not a copy of the intake decision into applicability data.

revision.description: VCS revision the intake record was read at, for a register identified by revision rather than by recorded_at.

scope.description: Same pool as instruction-intake.md §7 and agent-instruction-identity.md §4: reused, not paralleled. This is the currently recorded scope of the authoritative intake record. When the owner has decided a target scope that this recorded value conflicts with and the new append-only intake record does not exist yet, the recorded value stays here and status is "unresolved" (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §4).

repository.description: Repository identifier from the Instance inventory that this norm applies to. Required when scope is repository and forbidden otherwise. Distinct from norm.repository: the two happen to agree in the common case and are not required to.

technology_profile.description: Stack profile identifier from stack-profiles.yaml. Required when scope is profile and forbidden otherwise.

product_domain.description: Value from a repository's semantic_areas in the Instance inventory. Required when scope is product-domain and forbidden otherwise.

activation.description: Same pool as instruction-intake.md's observed_activation. This is the axis the resolver checks, not a restatement of what the intake record already says; the two are expected to agree and are read from different files.

globs.description: Path masks, same vocabulary as sources.rules in registries/inventory/repositories.schema.json and the delivery-adapter masks named in agent-instruction-identity.md §4.1. Required when activation is path-glob and forbidden otherwise.

task_class.description: Required when activation is task-class and forbidden otherwise. Narrows applicability to specific work_kind values and, optionally, specific change_class values — the closed pools of standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §2 and §3.

change_class.description: Absent means the norm applies to every change_class within the listed work_kind values, not that it applies to none. change_class is meaningful only inside work_kind: change (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §3), so when it is present work_kind must contain "change"; it may also list other work_kind values, but a change_class with no "change" in work_kind (for example work_kind: ["assessment"]) is an incompatible pairing and is rejected.

source.description: Same three values the resolver output contract (registries/rule-resolution/resolver-output.schema.json) uses for applicable_norms[].source. Not the same pool as a protocol route's source (kernel | instance | repository, standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §7) — a norm and a route answer different questions and are not forced into one vocabulary because the words look alike.

status.description: This record's own runtime-applicability state (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §4). It has exactly these two values and is not the intake verdict. "resolved": the axes above decide applicability deterministically — this includes a record whose intake verdict is deferred, since a deferred verdict neither activates, disables, nor unresolves a norm. "unresolved": scope, activation, source or a conflict cannot be decided deterministically (for example a recorded scope that conflicts with an owner-decided target whose new append-only intake record does not exist yet); the resolver returns unresolved_applicability for this subject from this status, not from a missing record. "unresolved" requires this record's own resume_condition; "resolved" must not carry one.

resume_condition.description: The exact condition under which this one unresolved record is revisited — the applicability registry's own return condition, owned here, distinct from and not a copy of the resume_condition of the intake record reached through intake_record. Its own, not shared with any other unresolved record (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §9). Required when status is "unresolved", absent when status is "resolved".

recorded_at.description: When this applicability record was established or last synced to the norm it names. Distinct from intake_record.recorded_at, which dates the intake record this one points at. It is not a synthetic sequence number: two append-only records of one norm identity established or re-synced on the same day share this value, and the file order they happen to sit in does not order them (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §4).

supersedes.description: Optional. An explicit statement that this append-only record takes precedence over one earlier applicability record OF THE SAME NORM IDENTITY established or last synced on the SAME applicability recorded_at as this one. It is the only sanctioned way to order two records of one norm identity that share an applicability recorded_at (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §4, §9): without it such a set is fail-closed, and the intake verdict is never itself a precedence key (there is no hard-coded adopt-edition > deferred). The pointer reuses the exact record identity instruction-intake.md defines and §9 names — register + artifact (norm.path) + region (norm.region) + recorded_at + verdict — it does not invent a parallel identity or a free-text ordering rule. path and region here MUST equal this record's own norm.path and norm.region: supersession is within one norm identity, never across identities. Forbidden when source is kernel, for the same reason intake_record is: a norm that never went through intake has no intake-record identity to point at, and no verdict multiplicity to disambiguate. Every declared supersedes relationship is validated by the resolver before an authoritative record is returned — in the current greatest-date cohort and in every historical cohort of the norm group alike; only the greatest applicability recorded_at then determines which cohort is authoritative. The resolver fails closed when this pointer resolves, within the carrier record's own applicability recorded_at cohort, to no record (including when the carrier is alone on its date — a supersedes is never harmless stray data), to more than one record, to a record of another norm identity, to a record on another applicability date, to itself, when the supersedes edges of a cohort form a cycle, or when a cohort that declares any ordering leaves more than one un-superseded head.

register.description: Path to the instruction-intake/*.yaml register that carries the superseded record, relative to the Instance root. Same component as intake_record.register.

path.description: Artifact path of the superseded record. Must equal this record's own norm.path — supersession is only within one norm identity.

region.description: Declared region of the superseded record, present only when this record's norm carries a region. Must equal this record's own norm.region.

recorded_at.description: intake_record.recorded_at of the superseded record — one component of its intake-pointer identity, not the whole of it, and NOT the superseded record's applicability recorded_at. The resolver additionally requires the superseded record to share this record's own applicability recorded_at (§9); that is not restated here.

verdict.description: intake_record.verdict of the superseded record. It is a pointer component that picks one of possibly several same-date entries, not a precedence rank: the ordering comes from this supersedes statement, never from comparing verdicts.

revision.description: intake_record.revision of the superseded record, for a register identified by revision rather than by recorded_at. When present the resolver requires it to match too.
